blocks: Biological foundations: cells, organisms and diversity
Both develop academic learning, reflection and personal study direction. UCR also includes writing and civic engagement.
Both study animal diversity and classification. UCR surveys the whole tree of life, including plants and microorganisms, rather than reproducing the dedicated animal sequence.
Both study population dynamics, competition, predation, communities and biodiversity, with ecological modelling. UCR extends across ecosystem processes and uses simple models in R.
Both study microbes, host defence, innate/adaptive immunity and immune mechanisms; UCR emphasises infection and immunopathology.
Both examine animal behaviour and its biological mechanisms. UCR approaches these through comparative nervous-system anatomy, physiology, regulatory behaviour and research models.
Both introduce cell structures, membranes, signalling, division and their molecular basis. The UCR course is a broader biomedical foundation.
Both study animal structure, function and regulation. UCR concentrates on adult human physiology and does not supply the plant component.
Both study inheritance and genetic variation. UCR applies these to human disease and genetic diagnosis rather than the maize phenotype experiment or full introductory chromosome-mapping sequence.

Molecular, cellular, physiological and biomedical biology

Both study DNA replication/repair, gene expression, cellular regulation and research approaches. Leiden additionally has a dedicated recombinant-DNA laboratory; UCR integrates molecular targets and cellular mechanisms.
Both study biomolecular structure and biochemical reactions. UCR emphasises enzymes and metabolism; Leiden also introduces general chemical concepts, acid–base reasoning and titration.

Both develop hands-on laboratory formation, experimental technique, reproducible records and scientific reporting. UCR uses biochemical, microbial and molecular investigations rather than the identical introductory exercises.
General data and machine-learning courses do not reproduce this genomics/transcriptomics/proteomics and biological-network integration course.
UCR does not supply a dedicated animal-and-plant developmental-biology sequence.
No separate selected UCR course establishes this additional requirement at its specific scope; related subject or method contributions are already placed once at their strongest counterpart.
Evolution, ecology, conservation and environmental systems

Both examine human impacts on species, habitats and biological communities and the scientific basis of nature protection. UCR focuses on biodiversity loss and conservation planning rather than the whole environmental-biology field.
Both develop evolutionary mechanisms, genetic variation, adaptation, speciation and evolutionary history; UCR does not reproduce every advanced Leiden application.

Both develop communication of biological research to a wider public. UCR’s substantial marine-biology outreach project supplies this shared educational function; Leiden has a dedicated course analysing communication forms and producing a popular-science article.
Quantitative methods, research and open study space

Both develop mathematical descriptions and dynamic models of scientific processes. Leiden applies stochastic, discrete and continuous models in R to biology; UCR uses general calculus, differential equations and a model project in Mathematica.
Both develop probability and statistical inference for research. UCR emphasises mathematical statistics and simulation; Leiden additionally teaches practical R regression and reporting.

Both teach experimental design and multivariable/generalised models, categorical outcomes, assumptions and R analysis. UCR examples concern health and behaviour rather than the full range of biological research.
Governance or general research skills do not reproduce the dedicated bioethics and responsible-scientist sequence.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers Leiden Biology's molecules-to-ecosystems identity. Two direct programme-interest clusters support coherent, substantially distinct alternatives: molecular/cellular biology linked to health and computation, and ecology/evolution/conservation linked to environmental change. All three retain feasible 24-course schedules and differ well beyond the four-course minimum. Production stops at the maximum of three defensible alternatives.

notes.text: Leiden Biology requires a broad first year, a 47-EC second-year Biology specialisation with molecular, organismal, evolutionary and ecological work, and a third year containing 30 EC of open choice plus a 24-EC Bachelor Research Project. UCR can assemble broad, molecular/biomedical and ecology/evolution programmes from current courses, but it does not reproduce Leiden's full organismal and field sequence or the required 24-EC research project; shared rows show substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.

audience.programmeDescription: Biology at Leiden studies living systems from molecules and cells to organisms, evolution and ecosystems. This comparison follows the broad Biology specialisation, with substantial laboratory, quantitative and research training.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programmes offer three biological emphases: a broad combination, molecular and biomedical biology with computational methods, or ecology and environmental change. Leiden provides more dedicated plant, developmental and systems biology, a structured Biology elective programme and a required full-time research project. The UCR methods and laboratory courses do not imply completion of that project.

curriculum.limitation: The pathway totals 180 EC: 60 EC in year one; 30 EC of compulsory study and 30 EC of restricted Biology choices in year two; and 30 EC of open study, 6 EC of methods and academic skills, and a 24-EC research project in year three. Biology choices follow five teaching blocks. Their possible subjects are choices, not compulsory additions.

componentNotes.y2-biology-profiling: 30 EC chosen from the Biology elective list across five blocks of four to five weeks. Select one available option per block; the list includes molecular, microbial, organismal and ecological subjects and field research.
componentNotes.y3-bachelor-project: Required 24-EC project, normally 1 March to 2 July 2027: 90 full-time working days. All first-year courses must be passed. Projects normally use a Leiden biological or affiliated institute; external projects require discussion with the study adviser and examination-board approval. Students may work in pairs but write individual English reports. September starts require an approved adjusted study plan.
componentNotes.y3-general-research-skills: Required 2-EC research-skills course, with assignments during the research project. September participation requires an approved adjusted study plan.
componentNotes.y3-statistics: Required 3-EC Statistics 2, normally completed in February before the research project begins. September participation is restricted to approved adjusted plans or a resit.
componentNotes.y3-elective-space: 30 EC in the first semester for a minor, exchange or self-chosen approved course package.
